newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu ends static, money market higher.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu ends static, money market higher.

text.p: Romania's leu closed Friday flat at 6,950/7,050, regaining early loses made in an interbank market facing shortages as most hard currency holders awaited weaker prices.
Short-term rates soared to 110-120 percent on a cash-starved money market, reacting to a rise in the average auctioned credit rate to 125.45 percent from a 90 percent.

Traders said they were digesting news the government plans to cut the budget gap to 4.5 percent of GDP this year from 5.8 percent in 1996 and to slash the 1997 trade deficit to $1.4 billion from last year's $2.5 billion.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea gave the forecasts on Friday without further details on the reforms package, which his centrist coalition government had discussed with international lenders.
The government is seeking up to $1.0 billion in total loans from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, which withheld credits to Romania last year.
Traders were keen to get further details of the full package, which Ciorbea is expected to announce next Monday.
"Those targets might be achieved, but we are still waiting for more details," said a trader with a dealer bank.
Operators saw continued pressure on the leu after which the market failed to attract any significant amounts of hard currency this week.
"We are waiting for new lows. The interbank leu might hit 8,000 to the dollar by end-February on the back of inflationary fears and scarce dollar offer," said one trader.
The interbank leu dipped about 8.5 percent this week, when it closed some 70-percent lower against its January 1 level.
Leu-dollar retail prices bobbed at 7,600/8,200, with licensed money changing bureaux reluctant to sell dollars.
